plain_english: Turn to these quieter, safer, more important activities. Do you really think there's any comparison between checking that grain gets stored in public warehouses without being stolen or ruined by careless importers — making sure it doesn't get damp or overheated, and that it weighs what it should — and beginning to study sacred and divine knowledge? This study will teach you what the gods are made of, what gives them pleasure, where they live, what they look like. It will show you what changes your soul can expect, where Nature will place us when we leave our bodies, what force holds the heaviest parts of our universe in the center and suspends the lighter ones above, puts fire at the top, and makes the stars move in their courses — along with many other wonderful mysteries. Won't you stop crawling around on earth and turn your mind's eye to these topics? While your blood still flows quickly and before your knees grow weak, you should take the better path. On this road, many good things wait for you: love and practice of virtue, freedom from destructive emotions, knowledge of how to live and die, deep peace. The situation of all busy people is miserable. But most miserable of all are those who don't even work on their own affairs. They have to time their rest by someone else's sleep, their walks by someone else's pace. Even their love and hate — the freest things in the world — are controlled by others. If such people want to know how short their lives are, let them think about how small a fraction of their time is actually their own.
original_excerpt: Betake yourself to these quieter, safer, larger fields of action: do you think that there can be any comparison between seeing that corn is deposited in the public granary without being stolen by the fraud or spoilt by the carelessness of the importer, that it does not suffer from damp or overheating, and that it measures and weighs as much as it ought, and beginning the study of sacred and divine knowledge, which will teach you of what elements the gods are formed, what are their pleasures, their position, their form? to what changes your soul has to look forward? where Nature will place us when we are dismissed from our bodies? what that principle is which holds all the heaviest particles of our universe in the middle, suspends the lighter ones above, puts fire highest of all, and causes the stars to rise in their courses, with many other matters, full of marvels? Will you not[10] cease to grovel on earth and turn your mind’s eye on these themes? nay, while your blood still flows swiftly, before your knees grow feeble, you ought to take the better path. In this course of life there await you many good things, such as love and practice of the virtues, forgetfulness of passions, knowledge of how to live and die, deep repose. The position of all busy men is unhappy, but most unhappy of all is that of those who do not even labour at their own affairs, but have to regulate their rest by another man’s sleep, their walk by another man’s pace, and whose very love and hate, the freest things in the world, are at another’s bidding. If such men wish to know how short their lives are, let them think how small a fraction of them is their own.
source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 19
